description:
Found by the HexDocs cold test (defk-djy.9, docs/cold-tests/hexdocs-entropy.md, point 8). Counting bytes (a 256-bin histogram, per window or over a whole binary, then Shannon entropy) is a common job with no catalog entry and no docs/performance.md entry, so building a fair optimised Elixir baseline meant guessing (:counters, 8 bytes per binary-pattern step from performance.md 2.2/2.3, results appended to a binary per 2.1). The cold tester's own numbers (in the log, loaded machine, not a catalog measurement): first pass bin_to_list |> Enum.frequencies 9 MB/s; :counters + 8-byte steps 138 MB/s; kernel ~2250 MB/s (16x, one process vs one call, not split over schedulers).

Done when examples/ has a byte-histogram (and windowed-entropy) example in the usual shape (Defk.Bench.report, expected verdict declared before the numbers, realistic size declared), the Elixir side tries at least Enum.frequencies, :counters/:atomics, a tuple of counts, binary-pattern steps of 1 and 8 bytes and a split over all schedulers, the kernel is compared one process vs one call and over all schedulers, and docs/performance.md gets an entry (section 2, 'counting bytes') with numbers, conditions and status; measuring.md's pointer to '2.12 Dense counters' is updated to the new entry if it is the better one.
title: Catalog: byte histogram and windowed entropy, with optimised Elixir baselines
